data.name: Pravin
data.gender_notes: Pravin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is clear, pure, shining and bright, especially someone who has the power of clarity and insight. The name Pravin carries the meaning “Shining, Bright, Clear, Pure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pravin usually hope their child will grow to embody shining, bright, clear, pure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who seek clarity in their spiritual journey, it signifies the inner light that guides us towards our true purpose in life.
data.etymology: Pravin belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shining, Bright, Clear, Pure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pravin total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Pravin represents the inner light or pure consciousness that exists within every individual. It emphasizes the importance of seeking clarity, gaining knowledge, and striving for a life filled with truth and insight. The name Pravin is a reminder that true wisdom and understanding come from within, that one must keep their consciousness clear and pure, and that the quest for knowledge and truth is a lifelong journey.

historical_references.reference: Pravin was a famous mathematician in ancient India who contributed significantly to the development of algebra. He lived during the Gupta Empire (circa 4th to 6th century AD) and is considered one of the pioneers of algebraic mathematics in India.

Another Pravin is mentioned in Indian mythology as the name of a demon king who ruled over the underworld. He is described as a powerful and fearsome figure who was vanquished by the god Indra. The time period for this reference is uncertain, but it is believed to be from the Vedic period (circa 1500-500 BCE).
